context: CPU flame chart profiler showing 855 stack frames across 8 modules (core, http, database, auth, cache, logging, scheduler, io), rendered on canvas with click-to-zoom subtree navigation, scroll-to-zoom, LOD labels, and hover tooltips.
first_impression: The bottom 4-5 rows are clearly readable with labeled frames, but the upper portion collapses into an unreadable rainbow wall of slivers at the default 1.0x zoom — which is expected and addressed by the interaction model.
what_works: The LOD system (3 zoom levels with hysteresis) correctly suppresses labels on sub-pixel frames and reveals them progressively on zoom, keeping the readable rows informative without clutter; the 8-color Tol bright palette is perceptually distinct and the compact legend maps quickly to frames.
what_doesnt: At the initial 1.0x view, the upper ~6 rows are a dense noise field of colored slivers with no readable labels — a first-time viewer has no obvious entry point and must discover that clicking zooms in; animation/interaction quality cannot be fully assessed from a static screenshot, but the rAF-throttled canvas redraw and 500ms zoom transitions appear well-structured in code.
